crubit.stdout:
Generates C++ bindings for a Rust crate

Usage: cc_bindings_from_rs [OPTIONS] --h-out <FILE> --rs-out <FILE> --crubit-support-path-format <STRING> [-- <RUSTC_ARGS>...]

Arguments:
  [RUSTC_ARGS]...
          Command line arguments of the Rust compiler

Options:
      --h-out <FILE>
          Output path for C++ header file with bindings

      --cpp-out <FILE>
          Output path for C++ implementation file with bindings

      --h-out-include-guard <STRING>
          Include guard for the C++ header file with bindings

      --rs-out <FILE>
          Output path for Rust implementation of the bindings

      --crubit-support-path-format <STRING>
          This is the format to `#include` Crubit C++ support library headers, using `{header}` as the  placeholder. Example: `<crubit/support/{header}>` will produce `#include <crubit/support/hdr.h>`

      --crubit-debug-path-format <STRING>
          Format specifier for path cross-references in "Generated from" comments.
          
          This can be used to create clickable links to the generated code, if you have a code navigation system like SourceGraph or CodeSearch.
          
          1. {path} is the placeholder for the path to the original Rust source file. 2. {line} is the placeholder for the line number in that file.
          
          This is only used for real files on disk. Virtual files have a hardcoded format.
          
          If None, uses the default format used for virtual files.

      --clang-forma

optional_tools_not_selected.cargo: Generated GN invokes rustc directly; no selected action invokes Cargo. Rust build.rs binaries are GN targets.
optional_tools_not_selected.Java: No selected subprocess action invokes Java or javac; platform is Linux and Android targets are excluded.
optional_tools_not_selected.Perl: No selected subprocess action invokes Perl; NASM helpers are generated by GN.
optional_tools_not_selected.host_git_for_dawn_version: Dawn version generator receives the pinned Chromium gpu/webgpu/DAWN_VERSION file; Git fallback is not selected.

limitations: Python AST inspection and argument tracing identify selected subprocess references, not every possible dynamic dependency.
Version/help probes and existing helper binaries do not establish successful engine compilation.
The full preflight integrates Python module and source inventory checks separately.
